children.text: Alex is a veteran full-stack engineer and educator with over 10 years of experience building modern web architectures and production systems at scale.
Sarah specializes in containerization, Kubernetes, and automated deployment workflows for large-scale distributed systems.
Marcus is an open-source contributor and systems expert focusing on type theory, compiler tooling, and high-performance applications.

title: Fundamentals of Next.js App Router
summary: Deep dive into the file-system based routing, nested layouts, and route groups in Next.js App Router.
keyPoints: Understanding app directory folder conventions
Creating nested layouts and error boundaries
Route groups and private folders
proTip: Use parallel routes (@modal) alongside intercepting routes (.) to create shareable modal dialogs without losing page context.

resources.title: App Router Cheat Sheet
resources.description: Visual quick reference for routing conventions

resources.title: Starter Repository
resources.description: Full starter code with nested layouts

children.text: The Next.js App Router introduces a paradigm shift in React web development. By organizing pages around file-system hierarchies, developers gain built-in support for nested layouts, streaming, and server-first rendering.

title: Server Components & Streaming Architecture
summary: Master React Server Components, Suspense boundaries, and progressive HTML streaming.
keyPoints: Differences between Server and Client Components
Eliminating client-side bundle weight
Progressive streaming with Suspense boundaries
proTip: Keep client components as low in the component tree as possible (leaves of the tree) to minimize JavaScript payload.

resources.title: RSC Mental Model Guide
resources.description: Comprehensive breakdown of Server vs Client components

children.text: React Server Components execute entirely on the server and never ship their dependencies to the browser. Combined with Next.js streaming, you can render static skeletons instantly while slower database operations stream in asynchronously.

title: Data Fetching & Server Actions
summary: Learn async data fetching, mutations with Server Actions, optimistic UI updates, and error handling.
keyPoints: Native fetch caching extensions in Next.js
Defining server actions for secure mutations
Optimistic UI updates with useOptimistic
proTip: Always validate server action inputs using Zod on the server side before executing database queries.

resources.title: Server Actions Sample Code
resources.description: Example patterns for CRUD server actions with Zod

children.text: Server Actions allow you to run asynchronous code directly on the server invoked seamlessly from client or server forms without manually configuring API endpoints.

title: Advanced Caching & Revalidation
summary: Demystifying the 4 caching layers in Next.js: Request Memoization, Data Cache, Full Route Cache, and Router Cache.
keyPoints: Navigating the 4 distinct Next.js caching layers
Time-based revalidation (ISR) vs tag-based revalidation
Cache tags with revalidateTag
proTip: Use tag-based revalidation (revalidateTag) for immediate on-demand content updates triggered by webhooks.

resources.title: Next.js Caching Architecture Diagram
resources.description: High-resolution flowchart of all 4 caching layers

children.text: Understanding how Next.js caches data, routes, and responses is critical for building blazing-fast applications that stay synchronized with your CMS.

title: Container Basics & Dockerfile Anatomy
summary: Understanding images, layers, caching, and building multi-stage containers.
keyPoints: Differences between virtual machines and containers
Layer caching mechanisms in Docker builds
Writing optimal multi-stage Dockerfiles
proTip: Order Dockerfile commands from least frequently changed to most frequently changed to maximize build cache hits.

resources.title: Dockerfile Best Practices
resources.description: Guide to minimal image sizes and fast build times

children.text: Containers package an application alongside all its dependencies and runtime environment, ensuring identical behavior across local machines and cloud clusters.

title: Docker Compose for Multi-Container Apps
summary: Orchestrating microservices, networks, and persistent volumes with Docker Compose.
keyPoints: Defining services, networks, and volumes in compose.yaml
Managing environment variables and secret files
Hot-reloading local dev environments in containers
proTip: Use named volumes for database persistence and bind mounts for fast local hot-reloading.

resources.title: Docker Compose Starter Configs
resources.description: Templates for Node.js, Postgres, and Redis setups

children.text: Docker Compose simplifies multi-service orchestration with a single declarative configuration file, enabling one-command development environments.

title: Production Hardening & CI/CD Pipelines
summary: Security scanning, rootless containers, and automated builds in GitHub Actions.
keyPoints: Vulnerability scanning with Trivy and Docker Scout
Running unprivileged non-root user containers
Automated multi-arch builds (amd64/arm64) in CI
proTip: Never run containers as root in production; explicitly create and switch to a non-privileged user inside the Dockerfile.

resources.title: Container Security Checklist
resources.description: Actionable hardening rules for production container deployments

children.text: Hardening production containers prevents privilege escalation attacks and guarantees fast, reliable builds across multiple target architectures.

title: Advanced Generics & Conditional Types
summary: Master conditional types, distributive patterns, and infer keyword in TypeScript.
keyPoints: Generic constraints with extends
Distributive conditional types over union types
Type extraction with the infer keyword
proTip: Wrap types in square brackets [T] extends [any] when you want to prevent unwanted distributive behavior over union types.

resources.title: TypeScript Advanced Type Gymnastics
resources.description: Cheatsheet of conditional type patterns and utilities

children.text: Conditional types allow you to express non-uniform type relationships, enabling library authors to construct ergonomic, fully type-safe APIs.

title: Mapped Types & Template Literal Types
summary: Craft dynamic, strictly-typed schemas and utilities with key remapping and template literals.
keyPoints: Iterating over keys with in keyof
Key remapping using the as operator
Template literal types for route and event typing
proTip: Use template literal types to enforce strict string formats like kebab-case, camelCase, or API route paths.

resources.title: Type Utilities Reference
resources.description: Handcrafted utility types for practical application development

children.text: Mapped types transform existing object properties into new types, unlocking deep immutability, validation wrappers, and reactive state handlers.
